exEn: He's looking for work in healthcare.
note: A bit formal; in everyday speech people say jobb: på jobbet = at work.

exEn: I've got a new job!
note: Same form in the plural: ett jobb, två jobb.

exEn: She wants to change careers.
He works for a big company.
note: Same form in the plural: ett företag, två företag.

exEn: My workplace is near the station.
We get paid on the 25th of every month.
note: Payday (lönedag) in Sweden is usually the 25th.

exEn: I have to ask my boss first.
note: False friend: a chef (cook) is en kock. Ch is said like sj.

exEn: I have lunch with my colleagues.
note: The plural kolleger is also correct. Stress on -le-.

exEn: She's employed at a bank.
note: Also used as a noun: en anställd (an employee), de anställda (the employees).

exEn: My employer is paying for the course.
note: Literally 'work giver'. The g in -givare is soft, like j.

ex: Det var många {kunder} i butiken idag.
exEn: There were a lot of customers in the shop today.

ex: Jag sitter i {möte}, kan jag ringa dig sen?
exEn: I'm in a meeting, can I call you later?
note: Sitta i möte = to be in a meeting. The verb is möta (to meet).

exEn: I work full-time at a warehouse.
note: Jobba heltid = to work full-time; a full-time job is ett heltidsjobb.

exEn: She works part-time while she's studying.
note: Jobba deltid = to work part-time; a part-time job is ett deltidsjobb.

exEn: We had to work overtime all week.

ex: Han har varit {arbetslös} i ett halvår.
exEn: He has been unemployed for six months.
note: Arbetsförmedlingen, the public employment service, helps people find work.

exEn: She's on sick leave for the rest of the week.
note: After seven days off sick you need a doctor's note (läkarintyg).

exEn: My husband is on parental leave this spring.
note: Swedish parents share 480 days of paid parental leave per child.

ex: Du kan {ansöka} om jobbet via vår hemsida.
exEn: You can apply for the job on our website.
note: Ansöka om + noun. In everyday speech people just say söka: söka jobb.

exEn: I sent my application yesterday.
note: Irregular: the definite form is also ansökan, and the plural is ansökningar.

exEn: I'm nervous about the interview tomorrow.
note: Stress on the last syllable: inter-VJU.

ex: Skicka ditt {CV} och ett personligt brev.
exEn: Send your résumé and a cover letter.
note: Said like the letters: 'say-vay'. A cover letter is ett personligt brev.

ex: Har du {erfarenhet} av att jobba med barn?
exEn: Do you have experience working with children?
note: Erfarenhet av = experience of or with. An experience you live through is en upplevelse.

exEn: The company is going to hire ten new people.

ex: Hon har fått en fast {anställning} på skolan.
exEn: She has got a permanent job at the school.
note: Fast anställning = permanent job; tidsbegränsad anställning = temporary job.

exEn: The factory laid off a hundred people.
note: Also to cancel a contract: säga upp lägenheten. Being fired is få sparken (informal).

ex: Han {sa upp sig} och startade ett eget företag.
exEn: He quit his job and started his own company.
note: The pronoun changes: jag sa upp mig, hon sa upp sig. In everyday speech you can also say sluta.

ex: Jag gör {praktik} på ett hotell i tre månader.
exEn: I'm doing an internship at a hotel for three months.
note: Göra praktik = to do an internship or work placement, often as part of a course.

ex: Min pappa går i {pension} nästa år.
exEn: My dad is retiring next year.
note: Gå i pension = to retire; a retiree is en pensionär. Said 'pang-SHOON'.

exEn: I'm taking Friday off.
note: The g in ledigt is silent. Vara ledig = to be off work.

ex: Min första {uppgift} var att svara i telefon.
exEn: My first task was to answer the phone.
note: Also means information or details: personuppgifter = personal details.

exEn: The hotel staff were really friendly.
note: False friend: personal means staff. 'Personal' is personlig.

alt: What do you do for a living?
What do you do for work?
ex: Trevligt att träffas! {Vad jobbar du med}?
exEn: Nice to meet you! What do you do?
note: Answer without an article: Jag är sjuksköterska (I'm a nurse).

exEn: I work as a carpenter in Uppsala.
note: No article before the job: Jag jobbar som lärare = I work as a teacher.

exEn: She works as a doctor in the ER.
note: The official word; doktor is common in speech. Same form in the plural: två läkare.

exEn: The nurse is taking a blood sample.
note: Two sj-sounds: sjuk- and -skö-. Used for both women and men.

ex: Han jobbar som {undersköterska} på ett äldreboende.
exEn: He works as an assistant nurse at a care home.
note: One of the most common jobs in Swedish healthcare and elderly care.

ex: Jag har en tid hos {tandläkaren} på tisdag.
exEn: I have a dentist appointment on Tuesday.
note: Literally 'tooth doctor'.

exEn: Our teacher speaks slowly and clearly.
note: Same form in the plural: en lärare, två lärare. Definite plural: lärarna.

exEn: My wife is a preschool teacher.
note: förskola (preschool) + lärare (teacher).

exEn: My brother is a police officer in Gothenburg.
note: En polis = a police officer; polisen = the police. Emergency number: 112.

exEn: The firefighters came after five minutes.
note: Irregular plural like man: brandmän, brandmännen. Used for women too.

ex: Han är {kock} på en italiensk restaurang.
exEn: He's a chef at an Italian restaurant.
note: English 'chef' is kock; en chef is a boss!

exEn: She's an engineer and builds bridges.
note: The g is an sj-sound: in-sje-NJÖR.

exEn: There are lots of jobs for programmers.
note: Stress on -me-. Also common: utvecklare (developer).

ex: {Snickaren} bygger ett nytt kök åt oss.
exEn: The carpenter is building a new kitchen for us.
We have to call an electrician.
note: Same form in the plural: en elektriker, två elektriker.

exEn: I'm going to the hairdresser's on Saturday.
note: Klippa sig = to get a haircut.

exEn: My grandfather was a farmer in Småland.
note: Irregular plural with ö: bönder, bönderna.

exEn: You should talk to a lawyer.
note: Stress on the last syllable: advo-KAT.

ex: Hon jobbar som {säljare} i en klädbutik.
exEn: She works as a sales assistant in a clothing store.
note: From sälja (to sell).

exEn: The cleaners come every evening after six.
note: From städa (to clean). Job words in -are have the same form in the plural.

exEn: The bus driver said good morning to everyone.
note: Chaufför (driver) comes from French; ch is said like sj.

ex: Hon jobbar som {journalist} på en tidning.
exEn: She works as a journalist at a newspaper.
note: The j is an sj-sound, as in French.

exEn: She's a researcher at Lund University.
note: From forska (to do research). Rs is pronounced like sh.

ex: Hennes pappa är {konstnär} och målar tavlor.
exEn: Her dad is an artist and paints pictures.
note: A painter or sculptor; a performer (singer, musician) is en artist.
